runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with one win and one place from seven recent runs on similar Good ground; a dyed-in-the-wool hold-up performer who will find his rearmost position unavailable in this field, forcing him to travel further forward than ideal.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent type with a poor recent record including a tenth on this course over 8f last time — three places from twelve runs on similar going offers little encouragement and the recent form string of 877690 is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Has recorded one win and four places from twelve runs on similar ground so carries proven form credentials; by instinct a hold-up horse who will be shuffled into midfield given the volume of closers in this race, limiting his ability to deliver his typical late thrust.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Carries the fades-in-finish flag and has not hit the frame in any of five recent starts on Good or Soft; drawn into a shorter trip than the 12f-plus distances he has mainly contested and the combination of style concern and flagged finishing weakness makes this a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Topweight for a claimer, but boasts the eyecatching form line of 565281 and won over 8f on Good ground at the Curragh recently — the tongue tie is new but he races prominently and this pace map suits him better than most.

runners_data.name: Seti One
runners_data.note: Two flags for fading in the finish and a dismal recent sequence of 4000-0 over trips stretching to 12f; dropping in distance here but the finishing weakness and poor recent form make a positive reading very difficult.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with wins at 8f and 9f on Good ground and a consistent recent sequence including a win this month for the Adrian McGuinness yard; the hood goes on, he races prominently, and the controlled tempo set by Cosmic Funk is tailor-made.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good ground recently and earned a place again four days later, suggesting fitness is good; a hold-up horse by nature who will be unable to settle at the back in this contest and the step up in pace demands at 8f on this flatter trip is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Aurora Mist
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win at 8f on Good ground in her form — 71 days off the track is the main query; by nature a hold-up runner who will be squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, meaning she won't be tracking from her preferred berth.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride on this Harrington-trained three-year-old who won over 10f on Good ground; form at 8f on Good is just one place from ten runs but she races prominently, the pace structure here suits, and Foley is a key booking.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.note: Officially rated 120 but that appears to be a jumps rating — two runs on the Flat show finishes of 19th and 10th, and the fade-in-finish flag raises further concern; form and style profile give little cause for optimism here.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Unknown style flag suggests tactical flexibility; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-quality booking for the Meade yard, and four runs at 8f on Good or Soft show a degree of consistency without winning — the jockey may be the biggest positive.

runners_data.name: Magna Kotcha
runners_data.note: Three runs only, all in the bottom half of the field, and 87 days off the track; the fades-in-finish tag alongside a limited and unimpressive form base means this Meade three-year-old faces a steep ask on return.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with Colin Keane for G M Lyons — no horse is likely to contest the lead with him, and he can control the pace entirely; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers his own winning chance if the race is set up to benefit the tracking horses rather than the pace-setter himself.

races.paceDynamic: Cosmic Funk is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with Colin Keane aboard for G M Lyons, should stride to the front unchallenged and control tempo from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop over this mile trip on Good turf. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Darkdeserthighway, Usuario Amigo, Timandi, and Aurora Mist are all genuine hold-up types who cannot all get to the rear naturally and have been redistributed to midfield in the mapping, meaning the back of the field will be congested and those horses will not be tracking from their preferred position. Prominent types Minaun View, Land Of The Giants, Glamazon, and Go Out will be able to race closer to Cosmic Funk's even tempo without expending excess energy in a pace battle, as there is simply no rival to push the pace hard. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace — riders who can track the controlled tempo from second or third and produce a smooth, well-timed challenge into the straight will be ideally placed, while the true hold-up horses face a structural disadvantage given the field's composition.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Funk sets a measured tempo unchallenged and the race is decided by a prominent tracker producing a clean turn-of-foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: Cosmic Funk dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, allowing prominent stalkers to travel through the race on the bridle before the two-furlong pole triggers a sprint finish; horses with form at 8f on Good ground who can race just behind the pace have the race set up perfectly for them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types moves to press Cosmic Funk from the halfway point, lifting the tempo and forcing a decisive split in the field.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger pace develops as one of the prominent group accelerates into the turn, stretching the field and eliminating the hold-up horses whose late run simply arrives too late over this trip; the winner will be a horse with proven 8f Good-ground form who was travelling comfortably at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Challenges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a horse who travelled through midfield produces the strongest finish of all.
scenarios.body: A falsely steady pace causes bunching approaching the final furlong, creating a bunched sprint that allows horses who settled in the middle of the field some chance, though the redistribution of true hold-up types to midfield means this shape is structurally compromised in this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closer Lands Snatch
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Funk's controlled gallop is so slow that it turns into a sprint finish and a genuine hold-up runner produces a devastating late burst from the back.
scenarios.body: The race effectively becomes a dash over the final two furlongs, but the structural problem for this scenario is that most of the true hold-up horses could not get to their natural rear position and will not be far enough back to produce a trademark late run; only if unusually strong late pace develops does this shape become realistic.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Funk gets a completely uncontested lead — if Keane allows him to dictate an easy tempo, the race is set up for the prominent trackers and any strong-finishing hold-up horse will find the run comes too late.

Minaun View and Land Of The Giants both race prominently for the same McGuinness yard — watch for yard tactics or a potential squeeze if both attempt to track Cosmic Funk from positions two and three simultaneously.

Timandi ran just eight days ago and Aurora Mist returns after 71 days — monitor their market moves pre-race as fitness levels at opposite ends of the freshness spectrum could be decisive in a close finish.

The hold-up cluster of Darkdeserthighway, Usuario Amigo, Timandi, and Aurora Mist will likely occupy a congested midfield rather than the rear — jockeys on these horses may switch to a more prominent ride early if they recognise the structural compression developing.

Hazrama's official OR of 120 appears to be a non-Flat rating and should be treated with caution as a guide — two Flat runs yielding 19th and 10th make her form effectively unreadable against this field.

runners_data.name: Cromac Quay
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old who has finished second twice at this trip on good ground; Shane Foley retains the ride for Harrington, who has been in fair nick (1/31 over 14 days), and a 34-day freshener looks ideal at a mile.|

runners_data.name: Donna Time
runners_data.note: Unclassified in terms of mapped style, and her recent form figures of 7-6-2 over longer trips offer little encouragement stepping back to a mile in Listed company; Cleary's yard is 0/4 in the 14-day window.|

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's filly wears a tongue-tie and was solid when third at this trip on good last time; Wayne Lordan takes over and she must bounce back from a disappointing ninth at Listed level over ten furlongs.|

runners_data.name: Green Carrera
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's sole confirmed front-runner has won three of her last four races including back-to-back miles on good ground, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) signals she may be racing further forward than ideal if the prominent pack crowds her — her chance is real but slightly discounted by positional uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's filly arrives on the back of four consecutive wins over six and seven furlongs, so the step to a mile is the key question; Chris Hayes takes the mount and her sharp-end acceleration is the asset, though a stamina query at this level is genuine.|

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator who finished eighth in a mile handicap on good last time, but earlier form shows a win and a second over seven furlongs; Gary Carroll will need the pace to collapse late over this extra furlong for Pivotal Attack to get involved at 52 days since last seen.|

runners_data.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners_data.note: Pat Twomey's filly is a natural prominent racer whose last run produced a 13th over this trip on good — her true style cannot find space in this crowded pace map, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) means she is a compromised proposition even if racing wide enough to travel closer.|

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: The second Joseph O'Brien runner has a win on soft and placed on good over this exact trip, but form of 3-1-4-7 overall suggests inconsistency; Declan McDonogh rides and at 52 days absent a peak-fitness question applies.|

runners_data.name: Sky Watch
runners_data.note: Unclassified stylistically and the form figures — largely long-distance hurdle placings — make this the most opaque profiling exercise in the race; Colin Keane's presence is the main attraction, though her Going peg is noted as a hood wearer in the headgear column.|

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly is a genuine prominent type whose natural front-running instincts are squeezed out of position here; she won twice over seven furlongs on good/tapeta but a big field and full prominent slots mean she carries a meaningful style-fit discount (0.90) and must be treated as racing against her grain.|

runners_data.name: White Sand Beach
runners_data.note: An Aidan O'Brien hold-up filly who placed twice over this trip on good ground in the past but has produced strings of 8s since; she was running just two days ago, which raises a freshness concern, and the blinkers headgear may be seeking sharper early focus.|

runners_data.name: Wild Bessie
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly won over seven furlongs at Naas on heavy, but her STA and GOO form is poor (10th, 8th) and she carries a finish-fade flag; bumped back into a midfield-map role from her natural prominent style, her redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.93) and 72-day absence combine to make her a highly speculative runner.|

races.paceDynamic: Green Carrera is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle, is expected to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat mile at Killarney. Meriden and Cromac Quay are genuine prominent types who will push to track closely, while Drop Dead Gorgeous and Sinmara add further prominent presence, meaning the pace positions will be contested rather than handed out freely. This field contains more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around are all natural front-to-prominent types who are likely to be shuffled back from their preferred positions as the prominent slots fill up, effectively forcing them to race in an unnatural midfield role. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo and a clutch of prominent horses able to track efficiently, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace throughout and kick from a position of comfort, rather than deep closers who must produce a sustained late surge from behind a potentially slow-moving gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Prominent Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera dictates an honest but sustainable pace and the prominent trackers Cromac Quay, Meriden, and Drop Dead Gorgeous settle just behind without burning energy.
scenarios.body: Green Carrera's measured fractions leave enough in the tank for close-order horses to quicken off the bend, and those who have tracked efficiently throughout will have the positional advantage to assert in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster over-races early, the pace folds quickly in the straight, and genuine hold-up types Pivotal Attack and White Sand Beach close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A bunched, slowly-run affair that implodes late would negate the front-runners' positional edge and hand the race to horses making late ground; Pivotal Attack's eight-length gap last time on similar ground at this trip is the cautionary note, but the form figures suggest potential if the pace truly collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Redistributed Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent positions are scrapped for early, several natural front-runners are checked and forced wide, and one of the displaced horses — Quiet Mutiny or Wild Bessie — manages to secure cover closer to the pace than expected.
scenarios.body: A fractured early order could allow a horse that recovers quickly from positional disruption to effectively race prominent after all and benefit from the position it naturally wants; however, both Quiet Mutiny and Wild Bessie carry style-fit discounts and must be treated as materially compromised options for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Burst Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera sets an unusually dawdling pace that compresses the field and turns the race into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A slow-run mile would bring all runners into contention entering the straight, theoretically giving a sprinting type like Meriden — who has won four of her last five — or a fresh Drop Dead Gorgeous an edge with a sharp turn of foot at the death.

watchPoints.text: Green Carrera's ability to dictate uncontested is key — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle can establish a clear lead from the gates or whether Meriden and Cromac Quay press close enough to impose a faster pace that could compromise her stamina in the final furlong.

Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around are all being mapped out of their natural prominent positions — watch for early crowding or interference around the first two furlongs as these horses attempt to secure ground they instinctively want.

Meriden's four-race winning run has come exclusively over six and seven furlongs; watch whether she settles behind the pace or begins pulling for her head in the first half of the mile, which would be an early sign her stamina will be tested.

White Sand Beach ran just two days ago — watch her demeanour in the parade ring and early in the race for any sign of fatigue or flat body language that would explain an Aidan O'Brien runner on such a quick turnaround.

Pivotal Attack is the only confirmed hold-up horse with a realistic winning profile; watch whether the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a closing run, or whether a slow tempo leaves Gary Carroll with too much ground to make up in a race that never truly strung out.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo

runners_data.name: Young Churchill

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who won over 10f on heavy and has been placed three times at similar trips; Nicola Burns claims 5lb and the horse wears a hood, which could sharpen focus in a falsely-run affair.|

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder

runners_data.name: Vervain

runners_data.name: Alto Sax

runners_data.name: Voice Of Northeast
runners_data.note: Improved to 4th over 13f on good last time, which is the right trip, but has no wins on good ground and has been well beaten in most starts; a true hold-up type who will struggle to get its preferred ground at the back of a field like this.|

runners_data.name: Limestone Red

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-profile booking for a modest handicapper; the horse ran 2nd over 12f on good recently but is a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield, and the headgear note (hood) suggests it needs help to focus.|

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a dire recent record — 0 from last 5 including several last-place finishes — and carries the "fades in finish" tag; the style displacement into midfield does nothing to rescue a horse badly out of form.|

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Has experience over longer trips (16-18f) so the stamina base is solid, but has not won in its last 9 starts and fades in finishes; its natural position at the rear of the field is likely to be even harder to achieve in a slow-run race.|

runners_data.name: Fantasy Fara
runners_data.note: Finished 9th on good over 12f last run and has never won on good ground; carries the "fades in finish" concern and, pushed into midfield rather than the rear it prefers, Luke McAteer will have very limited options tactically.|

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, despite a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he is racing slightly out of role, Chris Hayes can slot him into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the front over this 1m3½f trip on good ground. With no other genuine pace horse to press him, the fractions are likely to be measured and sustainable, creating a true-run but not pressured gallop that tends to favour horses who can travel prominently and pick off the leader in the straight rather than those making up ground from far back. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Limbocall, Vervain, Alto Sax, Voice Of Northeast, Highway Sixty One, Monroe Dasher, Crypto Crash and Fantasy Fara are all genuine closers who cannot all get their natural position at the rear; those most likely to actually secure rear positions are the bigger-striding, more experienced hold-up performers such as Alto Sax and Kevin The Great, while others will be shuffled into midfield against their will. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours prominent racers who can track Tassarolo and quicken from a short distance, and horses that need a truly strong pace to generate their late run will find this tempo insufficient.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tassarolo Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but unhurried pace, allowing a prominent tracker to wear him down.
scenarios.body: Tassarolo dictates from the front at a pace entirely of his choosing, and a horse sitting second or third on his heels picks him off entering the final furlong without needing an exceptional turn of foot. Young Churchill and Deuteronomy both have the prominent-racing credentials and good-ground form to fill that chasing role and capitalise on the steady tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is generous enough to string the field out and a genuine closer gets a clear passage to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse who secures a position at the rear settles sweetly in the first half of the race and, with the leaders tying up from a modest gallop, produces a sustained run from two furlongs out to get up close home. Alto Sax's strong recent form and good-ground record make it the most credible beneficiary, while Kevin The Great has the class and trip experience to run on if given a clear passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the hold-up horses — shuffled into midfield — find themselves too close to the pace and trigger a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With most of the field compressed behind a dawdling Tassarolo, the race degenerates into a sprint over the final two furlongs and several midfield-placed horses launch together, making it chaotic. Arch Enemy, who won last time out and handles good ground, and Young Churchill both have the cruising speed from mid-division to benefit if it turns into a dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo or a horse that creeps up to join him very early simply is never headed and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: Tassarolo, if his trainer has him well-wound despite only one win in the last 19 starts, could exploit the total absence of pace pressure and simply ping clear going into the home straight unchallenged. Limestone Red, who wears a hood and has prominent-racing form, is the only other realistic candidate to sit tight on Tassarolo's back and steal a march on the field.

watchPoints.text: Tassarolo's early lead is the race's pivot — watch whether Chris Hayes goes straight to the front or is surprisingly slow away, as that dictates everything about the tempo and who benefits.|

Limbocall and Vervain are genuine hold-up types who will want to be last or second-last but cannot both achieve it — monitor their starting positions and early stall exits, as one of them will be forced to race prominently against their will.|
Alto Sax has been running well and Ben Coen is a sharp jockey — if it secures the rear-most position in a field of horses displaced forward, it could be the one true closer getting its natural run.|

Young Churchill and Deuteronomy are both prominent types drawn into what could be a comfortable stalking position just behind Tassarolo — if either sits second or third entering the straight, they are very well placed for the race shape.|

God Of Thunder, despite running for the same yard as Tassarolo (Denis Hogan), has faded in every recent finish on good ground at this course — its sectional data over the final two furlongs should be monitored as a benchmark for how much the pace tests the field.|

runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer at 6yo who has been well-beaten in five recent outings at 17f-20f on good, and with 0W0P from similar going and a weak recent form string, there is little evidence it can land a blow even in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Moyassr

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way

runners_data.name: Lagoon Nebula

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4yo tagged with a fade warning in the finish and an uninspiring form string of 60-00; trainer Morrison has 0 winners from 3 in the past 14 days and the 7lb claim from Adam Browne-Souza does not offset a horse that consistently fails to see out its races.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo with five consecutive placings at 12f-16f on good ground for Paul Flynn, including two wins at 13-14f; W J Lee is a strong booking at Killarney and the horse's entire profile — good ground, this trip, prominent style — is tailor-made for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Maarisha

runners_data.name: Sonic Invader
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse placed at 3/3/6 in recent outings at 14-16f on good ground for Noel Meade, and Colin Keane is a strong pilot; despite being shown in midfield on the map because of the crowded rear, this horse will likely track from further back in the race, meaning it depends on a true pace — which this race may not fully provide.

runners_data.name: Parish Express
runners_data.note: J S Bolger-trained 5yo returning from 65 days off with an uninspiring 770-0 recent record; all four recent runs on similar going produced 0W0P and despite being a natural closer, the long layoff, modest form, and redistribution from its true hold-up slot mean it faces stiff challenges finding the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden 4yo with a fade-in-finish flag and an OR of 61, having placed 3rd and 4th at 10f on good but never winning; its redistribution from the rear to midfield on the map reflects a field saturated with hold-up types, and the fade warning combined with a sprint-ish background at 8-10f makes 1m6½f a stamina query.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo prominent type with experience at marathon distances (22f), placing 2nd at 13f on soft; the Jack Cleary 5lb claim helps at the weights and the horse travels prominently, but 0W1P on similar going and an OR of just 58 at the foot of the handicap suggest it is here to make the pace rather than win it.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a fades-in-finish tag, showing one placing from seven career runs on good ground; the piastre headgear flag, redistribution from the true rear of the field, and STYLE_FIT of 0.90 all dampen optimism, though Donnacha O'Brien's yard is in strong form (4/16 in 14 days) and Chris Hayes is reliable.

races.paceDynamic: Lagoon Nebula is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field over 1m6½f on good ground at Killarney, and with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, it sets a controlled, sustainable gallop that keeps the race honest rather than truly searching. The prominent types — Baila Conmigo, Coulstys Way, Jurality, and Folly Beach — will slot in directly behind, forming a compact lead group that dictates a measured tempo through the middle stages. Several horses listed in midfield — Sonic Invader, Maarisha, Parish Express, and Celestially — are genuine hold-up types that have been redistributed from the rear because the field holds more true closers than the map can place; of these, Sonic Invader (strong recent form over this trip on good) and Jurality (already a prominent type with excellent good-ground course form) are the most likely to actually carve out their natural position. The uncontested, controlled pace that Lagoon Nebula creates over an extended trip strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the tempo, conserve energy, and outstay rivals in the closing stages — this is a race shape that rewards those who travel smoothly in the first three and kick from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula sets a steady pace and the horses immediately behind it travel comfortably through the race.
scenarios.body: Baila Conmigo, Jurality, and Coulstys Way sit within two lengths of the leader, expend minimal energy in the middle mile, and are best-placed to challenge from two furlongs out on a course where stamina and position matter; a modest tempo over this distance rewards those who never have to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lagoon Nebula Front-Runs
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula dictates a longer-range solo lead and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Lagoon Nebula goes clear in the final quarter-mile without being pressured, its front-running role over this trip on good ground suiting a horse that has won from off the front; it posted a career-best when winning at 13f on good and this unchallenged scenario plays to its strengths.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough early to string out the field and create a true test of stamina in the straight.
scenarios.body: Sonic Invader and Parish Express, true hold-up horses who have been shuffled forward on the map but will track from further back in reality, would benefit if a genuine gallop allows them to make sustained late progress; Sonic Invader's recent back-to-back thirds at 14f-16f on good ground and Colin Keane in the saddle give it the most credible late claim of any redistributed runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Winner Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace collapses in the straight and a horse that has been ridden patiently delivers a late thrust from an unexpected position.
scenarios.body: Moyassr, dropped back from sprint trips and most effective on good ground, or Celestially, who handles this going, could pick up the pieces if those up with the pace are exposed as having burned their advantage; this is the least likely shape given there is only one front-runner and the pace has nowhere to become truly fast.

watchPoints.text: Lagoon Nebula sets the pace entirely alone — if it gets an uncontested lead at a comfortable gallop, it may simply never be caught in a field where no other horse has the inclination to press it early.

Sonic Invader and Parish Express are genuine hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map but likely to settle further back in reality — watch their position from the start, as a slow pace will leave them with too much ground to make up in the straight.

Jurality has been placed in its last five outings on good ground at this trip range and W J Lee takes the ride — any move from the prominent group two furlongs out is likely to involve this horse and it should be tracked throughout.

Moyassr is ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle despite being campaigned at much shorter trips recently — watch whether he elects to ride it prominently or holds it up, as that tactical decision will define whether it features in the finish at all.

Devine Genius and Celestially both carry finish-fade flags — if either appears to travel well into the straight, note that both have a documented tendency to weaken late and may prove false dangers in the closing stages.
